title: embed-paging-bridge-http-semantics-stream-compat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compatibility bridge that makes the new embeddings + rerank endpoints behave like legacy clients expect: stable pagination cursors, normalized HTTP error semantics, and graceful handling of streaming/batched rerank responses. This ticket defines the product acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, migration notes for client libraries, and the behavior matrix for adapter translation logic.
background: We launched a new embeddings + rerank API surface that supports streaming partial rerank results, structured tool outputs, and cursor-first pagination. Several important customers (and older SDKs) still rely on deterministic cursor formats, Link headers, and a small set of documented HTTP error codes. Without a compatibility layer, they see intermittent client-side failures, broken pagination, and differing retry behavior. Engineering proposals now include either changing clients or introducing a bridge/adapter that normalizes responses. Given customer timelines, we will ship a compatibility adapter that preserves the new runtime benefits but presents legacy semantics to dependent consumers.
proposed_solution:
Build an API compatibility adapter (embed-paging-bridge) that sits in front of the new embedding/rerank runtime. Key responsibilities:
- Cursor normalization: accept legacy offset/cursor formats and emit canonical next_cursor and stable opaque IDs; support both Link header and body.next_cursor patterns.
- Error translation: map internal runtime errors to the documented HTTP contract (400/401/403/404/409/429/500) and include standardized error.code and error.hints fields for client consumers.
- Streaming compatibility: when the backend streams partial rerank results, the adapter will buffer up to a short window (configurable, default 200ms) to return chunked responses for modern clients, but for legacy clients it will optionally deliver a consolidated non-stream response (via feature flag).
- Idempotency & tombstones: ensure interrupted pagination surfaces a tombstone marker and retry hints so older clients can resume without data duplication.
- Opt-in/Opt-out via headers: clients can request strict-compat via X-Redwood-Compat: legacy or prefer-streaming to select behavior.
Implementation notes: adapter implemented as a lightweight service in the API layer with existing routing policy, feature-flag gating, and an extensive test harness that replays production traces.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts /embeddings and /rerank requests with legacy cursor query params (cursor, limit) and returns next_cursor in both Link header and response body for parity tests.
HTTP error mapping implemented and tested: internal runtime error codes are consistently mapped to documented HTTP statuses with stable error.code and human-readable error.hints.
Streaming fallback behavior: controlled by header or feature flag; when disabled, adapter returns consolidated responses within SLA for median payloads (p50 < 350ms for typical 64-result rerank).
End-to-end integration tests exercise cursor resume with partial stream interruption and verify no duplicate items or missed results across 3 retry scenarios.
Client SDK smoke tests (JS and Python) added to CI that validate both strict-compat and prefer-streaming code paths.
Canary rollout shows no regressions in per-route token-cost telemetry and error-rate on embed/rerank dashboards (compare to baseline week).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge adapter behind feature flag and run internal traffic (10% of requests) with prefer-compat header. 2) Run canary for 48h across two regions and monitor errors, latency, token-costs. 3) Open beta with select customers and update SDKs with opt-in header. 4) Default to compat for legacy-flagged tenants for 4 weeks, then evaluate switching defaults based on metrics and customer feedback. 5) Deprecation path: after 90 days of opt-ins, warn customers via Console and release notes before removing legacy mode.
migration_notes: SDK maintainers must add X-Redwood-Compat header when running in polyfilled legacy mode; provide convenience flag in JS/Python clients (compatMode: 'legacy'|'stream').
Guidance doc: examples for switching to streaming mode and handling partial results; include catch patterns for 429 vs transient 5xx errors.
Provide a script to translate legacy cursor tokens to the new opaque cursor format for one-time migrations for large customers.
Notify customers with active pagination usage via Console banner and email, include test checklist and upgrade timeline.
risks: Increased latency for strict-compat path if adapter buffers streams too long; mitigated by configurable buffer window and SLA gating.
Translation bugs could cause cursor misalignment leading to duplicate/missing items; mitigate with a replay test harness and property-based tests.
Customers may rely on undocumented semantics; require careful monitoring and direct outreach before defaulting behavior changes.
